draft.reason: The documentation explains that pods are managed as part of a fleet where they are automatically patched with higher service versions. Additionally, single service deployments in CI/CD do not remove existing services but only deploy new or updated ones, meaning a manually removed service will be restored during an upgrade or patch cycle.

claims.text: Pods are part of a fleet that is always patched with higher versions of services, which can restore services if a lower version or removal attempt conflicts with the fleet state.
The documentation states that higher versions of the same service deployed to the pod represent the expected fleet behavior.

Single Service Deployment is an in-factory mechanism for CI/CD that only deploys the new service generated and does not redeploy all services, but it operates within the constraints of the pod's provisioned versions.

The service version cannot be lower than the version the Pod was initially provisioned with, implying that the pod maintains a baseline state that overrides manual removals if they conflict with the provisioned version.

retrieved_sources.text:
The reviewed tag request contains the tags and selected application or service versions, but it does not contain a base-APPLICATIONBOM field. This is the gap addressed by the proposed change.

Saved CWB and one-off tags cannot be deleted through the current dashboard. Availability can also differ by service type and release configuration, so the UI and current release guidance remain the source of truth for whether a particular version is eligible for post-GA tagging.

### why-the-checks-should-remain-enabledWhy the checks should remain enabled

The published promotion and tagging check catalog marks both the lower-version check and the Version Audit as strictly enforced. The Version Audit prevents a service or application from being tagged when its app-package dependencies would not be available in the promoted content.

PipelineHub has configuration that can skip the audit during tagging, but using that switch to avoid the moving-baseline problem would remove a separate dependency-safety control. The working decision is therefore to keep the checks and give both baseline-dependent checks the correct one-off base APPLICATIONBOM.

Configuration Guide for ArtifactService Artifacts Deployment
retrieved_sources.text:
* + Teams have different priorities (speed vs test stability)
	+ Preserves current behavior by default (no surprise impact)

Single Service Deployment (In-Factory Testing)
----------------------------------------------

* As described above, Single service deployment is an **“in-factory” deployment mechanism** and is **supported for CI/CD workflows only**. It is designed to optimize developer velocity by enabling **faster iteration and validation cycles** & **not intended to represent the exact production patching behavior**
* This allows for faster deployment of your service enabling you for faster iteration & validation cycles.
* A new EnvironmentService API for Single Tenant CD deployments which has the following behavior
	+ Only the new service generated as part of CI/CD will be deployed (EnvironmentService will not redeploy all services in the Pod as opposed to traditional sideloading route)
	+ No checks/validations for versions of the service already deployed in the pod (higher/lower)
		- Note however that the service version cannot be lower than the version the Pod was initially provisioned with in which case the deployment will still fail 
			* eg: If the POD was provisioned with 2501, you cannot deploy a service with 2410 version
* This is the default behavior during CI/CD since
* There is a branch level property called "**Single Service Deployment**" which is true by default
